title: Token-granularity SLI plumbing, cross-region degrade graph, and adaptive shed controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Operators need fine-grained visibility into token-level latency behavior to diagnose regressions and make failover/load-shed decisions without overreacting to noise. This ticket implements end-to-end plumbing for token-granularity SLIs (p50/p95/p99 per token-position and per-model-variant), a cross-region degradation heatmap that surfaces correlated stalls, and an adaptive admission-shed control dashboard that ties SLI breaks to automated circuit policy suggestions. Scope includes telemetry schema updates, backend aggregation lambda, histogram bucketing policy, Grafana panels, alert rules, and a lightweight canary rollout for the metric consumers.
acceptance_criteria: Token-level SLI metric exported from runtime: token_latency_ms with labels {model, variant, region, token_index_bucket, request_priority}
Backend aggregation job computes sliding-window p50/p95/p99 for token_index_bucket and writes to metrics-store (prometheus/tsdb-compatible) every 30s
Cross-region heatmap dashboard that can show token_index_bucket vs region with anomaly overlays (Grafana-ready)
Alerting rule: token_latency_p99_cross_region_degrade fires when p99 increases > 3x baseline for 5m in two regions
Adaptive shed control panel shows suggested admission thresholds and allows toggling an experimental circuit policy (canary)
Load-testing with synthetic KV hit/miss permutations demonstrates stable SLO behavior under 2x production QPS and documented results
Documentation: instrumentation spec + rollout plan + runbook published in Confluence and linked from dashboard

decisions: Use coarse token_index buckets to bound cardinality and keep metric cardinality under budget — chosen 4 buckets after experiments.
Store aggregated SLIs in Prometheus remote-write TSDB for low-latency dashboarding rather than BigQuery to keep alerting latency <1m.
Anomaly thresholding uses historical rolling-median + robust-mad multiplier (x6) instead of fixed absolute thresholds to accommodate model upgrades.
Adaptive admission suggestions computed from recent p95 slope and kv-miss-rate heuristics; final enforcement gated behind canary flag in AdmissionManager.
Do not include request payload hash in metrics to avoid PII risks; instrumentation will only use model metadata and token_index buckets.
runbook_summary: If token-level p99 breaches are detected: 1) Verify KV hit-rate and recent deploys via dashboard; 2) Activate canary admission-shed policy for affected region(s) through Console (experimental toggle); 3) If degrade persists, failover routing to secondary region and open incident; 4) Collect debug traces (trace_id) and escalate to runtime on-call.
alerts: Token SLI - Cross-region P99 spike: fires when two regions have token_latency_p99 > 3x baseline for 5m
Token SLI - Single-region sustained tail: fires when p99 > SLA value for 10m and p95 slope > 30%/5m
Instrument ingestion lag: alerts if backend aggregation falls behind > 2 windows (60s)
dashboard_panels: Cross-region token heatmap (rows=token_index_bucket, cols=region) with p99 color map
Per-model-variant token percentile time-series (p50/p95/p99) with deploy markers
KV-hit vs token-p99 scatter with regression trendline
Adaptive admission control panel with suggested thresholds, historical impact simulation, and experimental toggle
Synthetic traffic comparison lane (90/50/10 kv-hit scenarios)
notes_on_instrumentation: To keep cardinality manageable we attach only {model, variant, region, token_index_bucket, priority}. token_latency_ms histogram uses exponential buckets tuned to observed percentiles (start=0.5ms factor=1.6 count=40). Aggregator computes sliding-window quantiles using TDigest to reduce memory footprint.
implementation_risks: Metric-cardinality blowup if additional labels are added by feature teams — mitigation: strict schema enforcement and automated cardinality alarms.
Prometheus ingestion pressure during traffic spikes — mitigation: rate-limiting on aggregator and remote-write batching.
False positives during model rollouts — mitigation: use rollout-aware baseline and progressive exclusion windows for 10m post-deploy.
